subject: Session artifact lifecycle and deletion paths for EU deployment
messages:
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@nordicbank.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nordicbank.com
Date: 2028-10-05T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default (requests, prompts, outputs)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our security and legal teams around default behavior for hosted vs VPC deployments:

1) For the hosted API, what exactly do you retain by default from a single session? Do you store the raw request, tokenized prompts, model-generated outputs, or only telemetry?
2) For Redwood Private deployed in our EU VPC, is there a different default retention window or is everything ephemeral unless we opt-in to logs?
3) If we ask for deletion (e.g., regulatory request or user erase), what is the end-to-end workflow and SLA — do you zero out KV caches, delete backups, and remove tombstoned indexes?

We need short, clear answers to include in our internal memo. If you can also attach your standard retention SLA, that would be helpful.

Best,
Sara Jensen
Head of Cloud Security
Nordic Bank
[Attachment: nordicbank-questionnaire-questions.docx]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@nordicbank.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-05T13:30:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default (requests, prompts, outputs)

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. I summarized below; see the attached SLA for formal wording and a short runbook we follow for deletion requests. Quick TL;DR first: hosted API retains minimal telemetry + 30 days of request/response artifacts by default (unless you opt-in or enable Private), while Redwood Private (VPC) defaults to ephemeral session caches with customer-controlled retention.

Details (hosted API):
- Default captured items: request metadata (timestamp, model_id, route, token counts), request body (raw text) and model response are stored by default for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. Prompts vs outputs are treated as request vs response artifacts.
- Retention window: 30 days by default for request/response artifacts; aggregated telemetry and non-identifying metrics retained longer for analytics only.
- Deletion path: when a deletion request is triggered (API call or legal notice), we mark artifacts for purge and initiate deletion across the serving runtime, KV caches, and long-term stores. There is a tombstone marker for 7 days to ensure downstream indexing systems converge; final physical purge completes within 14 days after tombstone. Backups are rotated and destroyed according to backup TTLs — we do not keep extra copies beyond retention windows.

Details (Redwood Private in EU VPC):
- Default capture: session caches (KV) are ephemeral and live on customer-controlled volumes. By default we do not send request/response artifacts to Redwood-hosted control-plane stores unless you enable "Diagnostics Uploads" or sign an opt-in.
- Retention window: if Diagnostics Uploads are disabled, there is effectively no centralized retention — the customer controls local retention rules. If you enable uploads, the default is 30 days unless contractually changed.
- Deletion path: for Private deployments we provide a deletion runbook and an API that can remove artifacts from the control plane; for customer-managed volumes we provide guidance and can run coordinated scripts under a support engagement to wipe volumes and rotate KMS keys.

Prompts vs outputs nuance: we consider the model prompt (what the user sent) as a request artifact and the generated content as an output/artifact. Both follow the same default retention and deletion paths unless you opt into a different pipeline (e.g., streaming-only, no storage). We can provide a configuration that drops outputs immediately after streaming if that suits your compliance posture.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-sla.pdf attached — it includes the formal timelines and a deletion runbook excerpt. Also attaching our short FAQ. If you want, we can convert select paragraphs into contract language for the SOW.

I'll loop in Karthik for the backup/key-rotation specifics.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-data-retention-sla.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-06T10:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default (requests, prompts, outputs)

Hi Sara — quick technical addendum on backups and KMS: 

- Backups & snapshots: our hosted control plane takes periodic snapshots for disaster recovery. Snapshots containing request/response artifacts are covered by the retention SLA; when artifacts are deleted, snapshots containing them are rotated out per the snapshot TTL (maximum additional exposure historically is one snapshot cycle ~7 days). We commit to deleting snapshot references to purged artifacts per the SLA timelines.
- KMS & key rotation: for hosted customers we encrypt at rest with customer-specific keys (when requested under enterprise plan) or Redwood-managed keys by default. For EU Private deployments we recommend customer-managed KMS so that key rotation/zeroization becomes a means to ensure irrecoverability after deletion.
- Tombstone explanation: tombstones are markers we place to coordinate deletion across caches, indices, and analytics pipelines; they exist briefly to ensure there are no stale copies. The tombstone window is configurable under enterprise contracts.

If you want specifics for our on-prem package (air-gapped), we can provide the scripted steps we run with a customer security engineer.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default (requests, prompts, outputs)

Hi Sara — following up with next steps so your legal/procurement team has clear asks: 

1) If you want "no default storage" for customer requests in Redwood Private, confirm Diagnostics Uploads = OFF in the SOW; we will include a clause that we will not ingest request/response artifacts into our control plane.
2) If you need hosted API but with shorter retention, we can offer 7-day retention for request/response artifacts as an addendum (requires an SLA amendment).
3) For deletion SLA in contracts: we suggest language stating tombstone period = 7 days, final purge within 14 days, and snapshot rotation within 30 days. We can provide exact legal wording — see attached spreadsheet where I've filled recommended contract clauses.

Next steps: I attached our filled questionnaire and the redlined clause suggestions. If procurement wants, we can set a short call to finalize contract language and KMS options.

Best,
Marissa Cole
